name: Flex Offense
idea: Pass across the top, cut along the baseline, screen down, and you're set up to do it all again on the other side.
why: The flex never stops. Every pass across the top starts the same two screens, so the defense has to stop the same moves again and again. Everyone takes a turn at every spot, so everyone learns every job.
tryit: Walk through it with no defense first. Say each job out loud: pass across, flex screen, flex cut, down screen. Then run it on the other side without stopping.

frames.say: This is the *flex*: two players at the top, two in the corners, and {5} on the block, on the same side as the ball.
*Pass across:* {1} passes over to {4}. That pass starts the flex.
*Flex screen:* {5} steps out from the block to set a screen for {3}.
*Flex cut:* {3} runs along the baseline, right past {5}, to the basket on the ball side.
*Down screen:* {1} runs down and screens for {5}, and {5} pops up to the top. The screener gets screened!
{1} slides to the corner. Look: everyone is in a flex spot again, just flipped. Now {3} is on the block.
{4} passes across to {5}, and the flex starts again on the other side: {3} screens and {2} cuts.
